# Blind validation of the frozen robot36dec decode against the Series 33 reference slides

The decoder ran without any access to these images (SPEC.md rule 2; FROZEN.md); this comparison was made afterwards (SPEC.md section 5 step 4) and scores the finished decode only. Nothing in this report was available to the decoder, and no number here feeds back into it.

## Summary (written by hand; every number below this section is regenerated by the tool)

**Protocol.** SPEC.md section 5 fixes the order: synthetic tests, real-recording tests, freeze (`FROZEN.md`,
`robot36dec/params_frozen.json`, 2026-10-04T20:32:31Z), and only then this comparison. The decodes scored here are the
frozen runs in `runs/real_normal` (normal path: VIS 8 found, line 0 at 323.7043 s) and `runs/real_recovery` (`--mode
recovery`, header ignored, line 0 at 323.7040 s), written at 20:26 UTC with the parameter file that was frozen unchanged
six minutes later (same sha256). The package contains no code that reads a reference image (`grep -ri "event_images\|slide" robot36dec/`
finds nothing; the word "reference" occurs there only as "reference recording" and "noise reference", and PIL is used
only to write the outputs); the references were opened for the first time by this tool, after the freeze. The reference set is every image in `../event_images/` (151 files: received copies of the 12 Series 33 slides,
received images of unknown slide, and non-slide distractors such as waterfalls and composites), minus the nine
`*_pipeline_*` files, which are decodes made by this project's own pipeline from other stations' audio of the same burst
and therefore not independent references (they rank at the top when included: `runs/validation/run1_with_pipeline.md`).
The primary reference for the block tables, `109_received_slide10_BI8SWK_1147_clean.jpg`, was fixed a priori as the clean
copy used in the earlier analysis (`REPORT.md` 2.2), so that the earlier numbers are comparable; the ranking itself is
over all references and does not depend on that choice. Nothing here feeds back into the decoder.

**Result.** Both paths identify **slide 10** ("Cosmonaut A. Kikina supports ARISS"): 13 of the top 19 ranks are copies of
slide 10 (the remaining six are the noisy / partial slide-10 copies, which rank just below), the best copy of any other
slide reaches a band 62-108 NCC of 0.53 against 0.93 for slide 10 (margin 0.40-0.42 in every decode). The whole-frame
margin is smaller (+0.10) because all twelve slides share the same layout (the "Student Education 2026" title bar in lines
0-20, a caption and callsigns in the lower half), which is also why the wrong-slide null of the top block is high
(mean 0.65): the title bar is not slide-specific evidence, the band 62-108 and the lines 20-62 are. The highest-ranked
file overall is `510_received_unknown_KC3YIP_samepass_1439` (a received image whose slide number is not in its name; its
band NCC of 0.55 and its time, 14:39 UTC, do not make it a slide-10 copy, and it is listed, not used).

NCC at zero shift against the channel-blurred BI8SWK copy; the three other named copies (`074_*DL7NDR*`, `060_*WA3LXD*`,
`099_*KU4YJ*`) give the same numbers within 0.01 (0.09 in lines 20-62 for the KU4YJ same-burst decode, which shares this
recording's fading). The lower block 108-240 is at its null in every decode (z 1.2 against the wrong-position null, 0.06
against a wrong-slide maximum of 0.08): the lower half of the slide is not in the recording, as established before. The
normal and recovery paths differ by at most 0.004 in any block (their timings differ by 0.3 ms), i.e. the decoder reaches the
same picture with and without the header. Compared with the earlier take2 numbers (0.87 / 0.65 / 0.93 / 0.06) the frozen
decoder gives 0.878 / 0.628 / 0.926 / 0.056: the same within 0.03, with ten more lines above the 0.5 per-line threshold
(lines 54-61 are now continuous with the band). The small best shifts (|dy| <= 1 line, |dx| <= 3 px, raising the NCC by
<= 0.005) confirm the timing solution of the decoder within one line and 3 px (0.8 ms).

curves). Per-line data: `runs/validation/VALIDATION_lines.csv`; full ranking: `runs/validation/VALIDATION_ranking.csv`.

## Method

* References: luminance, resampled to the Robot 36 frame (320 x 240, full frame, LANCZOS) and passed through the decoder's channel blur, a horizontal Gaussian of sigma 9 px (the 12 ms analysis window spans ~44 px); a 3-line vertical average is added only when the decoded image is a 3-line fused display. The decoded images are used as written.
* Statistic: Pearson correlation (NCC of mean-removed blocks) per line block top_0_20 = lines 0-20, mid_20_62 = lines 20-62, band_62_108 = lines 62-108, low_108_240 = lines 108-240, all = lines 0-240, at zero shift and at the best small shift (|dy| <= 3 lines, |dx| <= 4 px).
* Ranking: references sorted by the whole-frame NCC at zero shift; the best-matching slide is the slide label of the top reference; the margin is the gap to the best reference of any other known slide.
* Nulls: (a) wrong slide = every reference of another known slide at zero shift; (b) wrong position = the decoded block against the best reference, and pooled against every slide reference, at non-overlapping vertical positions (|shift| >= block height, 2-line steps, plus the horizontally mirrored reference; whole frame and blocks taller than half the frame: cyclic shifts 20-220 lines, plus mirrored); (c) control = the decoder's own pure-noise decodes against the best reference. z = (NCC at zero shift - null mean) / null sd.
* Per-line curve: NCC of each decoded line with the best reference at the whole-frame best shift; single-line null = pooled wrong positions (cyclic shifts >= 10 lines) of all slide references; "surviving lines" = 5-line smoothed NCC > 0.5.

## Interpretation

A block whose NCC exceeds the wrong-position null by several sigma and the wrong-slide maximum carries the reference picture; a block within the null is noise or an unrelated placement. The pure-noise control decodes show what the identical pipeline produces with no picture at all. Nothing in this report was available to the decoder.
